item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q006_ubiquitin_like_function_divergence","answer":"SCOPe supports remote homology between ubiquitin-related proteins (family d.15.1.1) and UBX domains: they are distinct families within the ubiquitin-like superfamily d.15.1 and share the beta-grasp fold d.15. This makes core-fold recognition and cautious structural-template use biologically useful, but UBX domains are generally noncovalent interaction/adaptor modules, often for p97/VCP, rather than ubiquitin-like covalent modifiers. Ras-binding domains are classified separately in the Ras-binding-domain-like fold/superfamily d.110/d.110.1; any ubiquitin-like architectural resemblance does not establish the same evolutionary or biochemical role. It would therefore be unsafe to transfer ubiquitin conjugation, E1/E2/E3 participation, or modifier status to a UBX domain, or Ras/small-GTPase binding to ubiquitin-related or UBX proteins. Interface, pathway, and substrate specificity also should not be transferred solely from a shared fold; those assignments require sequence/profile support and direct biochemical or binding evidence.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
